terms.meaning: A panel that slides in from the edge of the screen to show details.
How much of a person's record another user is allowed to see or change.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the family page
sections.what: Brings in icons, buttons, cards, the drawer panel, notifications, the API helper and routing. The icons hint at family management and sharing with doctors.
sections.why: Standard setup. Reason for each feature not stated in the code.

sections.name: FamilyMember
sections.title: Family member data shape
sections.what: Describes one family member: id, name, relationship, optional birth date, gender, photo and access level.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets the data shape for the family list. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Access level is typed as free text here, so valid values are not enforced by this type.

sections.name: DoctorShare
sections.title: Doctor share record shape
sections.what: Describes one doctor share link as the page receives it. It holds the token, optional doctor name and email, expiry date, whether it was revoked or has expired, how many times it was opened, and the full link.
sections.why: Gives the page a clear shape for share data so that fields are not guessed.
sections.watch_out: The page reads expiresAt as text, so the server must send a valid date string or the date display will fail.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 1)
sections.title: Loading family and share data
sections.what: When the page opens, it asks the server for family profiles and doctor share links at the same time. It stores the owned profiles, shared profiles and share links, and shows an error message if the request fails.
sections.why: Loading both lists together saves time, and the page can show both sections from one function.
sections.watch_out: If the response shape changes, the page quietly shows empty lists instead of an error, so missing data can look like no data.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 2)
sections.title: Adding and removing family members
sections.what: Sends the new member's name, relationship, optional date of birth and gender to the server, then closes the form and reloads the list. Removing a member asks the user to confirm in a browser prompt, then deletes the profile and reloads.
sections.why: Adding and removing use the same pattern: call the server, show a message, then refresh the list.
sections.watch_out: The removal confirmation is a plain browser prompt, which is easy to dismiss by mistake. Deleting also has no undo here.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 3)
sections.title: Creating and copying doctor share links
sections.what: Asks the server to create a time-limited link that lets a doctor view lab reports, prescriptions, vitals and the timeline. It then builds the full web address from the current site and stores it so the user can copy it.
sections.why: The link is made on the server and only the page address is added here, so the browser does not need to know any private details.
sections.watch_out: Copying uses the browser clipboard feature, which may be blocked on pages that are not served over a secure connection. The copy error is not handled.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 4)
sections.title: Page header and profile list
sections.what: Draws the page title and four buttons: Permissions, Doctor Share, Add Profile, and a count of managed profiles. Below it, the managed profiles appear as cards, or a message invites the user to add a family member when the list is empty.
sections.why: The header gives the three main actions in one place, and the card list shows each managed person.
sections.watch_out: The first letter of the name is shown as the avatar, so an empty name would cause an error when reading the first character.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 5)
sections.title: Loading spinner and empty state
sections.what: Shows a spinning icon while data is loading, then either the empty message or the grid of managed profiles. Each card shows a delete button.
sections.why: Keeps the page from looking empty while data loads.
sections.watch_out: The loading check and empty check run in a fixed order, so changing one can hide the other state.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 6)
sections.title: Member card details and caregiver link
sections.what: Shows each member's gender or Active Profile label and a Caregivers button that opens the permissions page.
sections.why: Gives a quick path from a person's card to who can see their records.
sections.watch_out: The gender text is shown in lowercase with only the first letter capitalised by style, so the displayed text may differ from the stored value.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 7)
sections.title: Profiles shared with you
sections.what: Shows a section only when other people have shared profiles with the current user. Each card shows the person's name, relationship and access level, which defaults to VIEW.
sections.why: Lets a caregiver see which profiles they can open, and only appears when there is something to show.
sections.watch_out: The access level text comes straight from the server, so a new level added there will appear without any styling.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 8)
sections.title: Add member form
sections.what: A drawer panel with fields for full name, relationship, gender and optional date of birth. The Add Member button stays off until a name is typed and while saving.
sections.why: Keeps the form in a side panel so the user does not leave the page.
sections.watch_out: Only the name is required here. The relationship and gender defaults are set in code, so a user who does not change them gets Parent and Female.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 9)
sections.title: Doctor share dialog and link result
sections.what: Shows a form for doctor name, doctor email, and how long the link should last. After creation, it shows the link in a read-only box with a copy button and a message explaining the doctor does not need an account.
sections.why: Lets the user create a link and copy it in one dialog.
sections.watch_out: The copy button shows a check mark for two seconds only. Closing and reopening the dialog clears the link, so the user must copy it first.

sections.name: FamilyDashboard (part 10)
sections.title: Doctor email, duration and footer buttons
sections.what: Lets the user enter an optional doctor email, pick 1, 7, 14 or 30 days, and see which resources are shared: lab reports, prescriptions, vitals and timeline. The footer has Close and Generate Link buttons.
sections.why: Lets the user decide how long the doctor can view the records and tells them what is included.
sections.watch_out: The doctor email is only stored, not checked here or sent by this page. The dialog does not tell the user whether an email was sent.

summary: Family page for managing relatives' health profiles, with icons that suggest sharing records with doctors. Only the setup and one data shape were visible, so most of the page is unclear.
purpose: Likely purpose from the icons and names: viewing and managing family members and sharing their records. This is inferred, not confirmed.
why: Reason not stated in the visible code.
how: Unclear from the visible sections. The file uses routing, notifications, API calls and a side drawer for details.
inputs: Unclear from the visible sections. Likely family member data from the API.
risks: The imports include share, copy and lock icons, which suggests the page creates ways to share health records. Sharing medical data is high risk, so the access rules must be checked before relying on it.
debug: Not enough is visible to give reliable steps. Review the remaining sections first.
